s: God dwells in the heart (as King and Emperor)
q: Who but the Guru can explain that the King and Emperor dwelleth in the heart?

s: God pervades everything (through love)
q: My Lord, who is dyed with love, pervadeth everything--

s: God is the Relisher
q: He Himself is the Relisher; He Himself is the relish

s: God is the Enjoyer
q: He Himself is the Enjoyer; He Himself is the robe; He Himself the couch and the Spouse--

s: God is the fisherman
q: He Himself is the fisherman and the fish; He Himself is the water and the net.

s: God is the fish
q: He Himself is the fisherman and the fish; He Himself is the water and the net.

s: God is the water
q: He Himself is the fisherman and the fish; He Himself is the water and the net.

s: God is the net
q: He Himself is the fisherman and the fish; He Himself is the water and the net.

s: God is the bait (within the net)
q: He Himself is the lead of the net; He Himself is the bait within it.

s: God causes to flourish the garden of the world
q: He is the Lord who hath caused the garden of the world to flourish and grow green

s: God restrains sea and land
q: And who restraineth sea and land; hail to the Creator!

s: God is the Creator (true and eternal)
q: He is, was, and shall be: He was not born, neither shall He die; True is the Creator.

s: the Name is a true wine (prepared without molasses)
q: The true wine is that which containeth the true Name; it is prepared without molasses.

s: the Name is pure
q: Pure is the Name; pure is the place of the true Cherisher.

s: the Name produces the nine treasures (from the name of the one God)
q: From the name of the one God the nine treasures are produced, and man obtaineth the marks of His favour.

s: the Name is man's support
q: Preserve me as it pleaseth Thee, O God; Thy name is my support.

s: God is a the One Giver
q: The Giver gave man a pill of the intoxicant illusion.

s: the Name is pure wealth
q: God's name is the pure wealth; God giveth it through the Guru.

s: the Name is equal to nothing (religious ceremonies are inferior)
q: Were I to perform hundreds of thousands and millions of religious ceremonies, all would not be equal to God's name.

s: the Word bestows honour (on one imbued with it)
q: The Pure One becometh not impure: he who is imbued with the Word obtaineth honour.

s: the Word cleanses the heart
q: The heart cannot be cleansed without the Word; from the True One truth is obtained.

s: the Word extinguishes the fire of desires
q: They who are preserved by the Guru are pure; the fire of their desires is extinguished by the Word.

s: the Word is a lamp (lit by the virtuous woman)
q: She lighteth the lamp of the Word, and weareth God's name as her necklet.

s: Guru gives the Name (as ladder, boat, and raft)
q: The Guru giving me God's name is my ladder, my boat, and my raft;

s: Guru is the lake
q: The Guru is the lake, the sea, and the boat; the Guru is the sacred stream.

s: Guru is the sea
q: The Guru is the lake, the sea, and the boat; the Guru is the sacred stream.

s: Guru is the boat
q: The Guru is the lake, the sea, and the boat; the Guru is the sacred stream.

s: God is true the True One
q: Nanak, know the True One alone as true.

s: Guru is the sacred stream
q: The Guru is the lake, the sea, and the boat; the Guru is the sacred stream.

s: Guru ferrieth man (across the ocean of the world when he looks with favour)
q: But the true Guru hath a vessel for the terrible ocean, and ferrieth over him on whom he looketh with favour.

s: Guru causes to meet God (through instruction)
q: Nanak, the true Guru, having taught me love, hath caused me to meet God, and I abide in His fear.

s: God's court is a place of honour
q: Man is known as properly intoxicated when he obtaineth a place in God's court.

s: God's court contains happiness
q: Nanak, make the true Guru' thy friend, and thou shalt obtain happiness in God's court.

s: man is a trader (in the world)
q: Trade, O trader, and take care of thy merchandise.

s: man is perishable
q: If I say I am perishable, it will not avail me; but if I really know that I am perishable, it will.

s: man has body (made from blood and semen)
q: Thy body made from blood and semen shall be brought to the fire at last.

s: man has soul
q: When the body falleth, the soul fleeth away; what shall be the condition of the evil doers?

s: man is saved by Guru (through God's name)
q: By taking the protection of the Guru man shall be saved; counterfeit is the capital of the perverse.

s: God bestows happiness (through service)
q: By serving Him man obtaineth happiness and proceedeth with honour to His court.

s: man obtains happiness (through God's name)
q: Happiness cometh to him who meditateth on the, Word; perfect happiness to him who is imbued with God.

s: man obtains honour (by remaining true)
q: Thy merits cannot be expressed by words; if man remain true, he shall obtain honour.

s: man dies Death (when his measure of life is full)
q: Even if thou be very learned thou must depart; none may remain when his measure of life is full.

s: mammon ruins woman (when she is separated from her Spouse)
q: Accursed is her life who is separated from her Spouse she is ruined by mammon.

s: mammon causes worldly attachment (in the perverse)
q: As a man goeth astray at night in his sleep, So doth he in whose heart there is pride and worldly love, and who is in the power of mammon.

s: truth is superior to everything
q: Everything is inferior to truth; the practice, of truth is superior to all else.

s: virtue brings happiness (through servitude to it)
q: O silly one, happiness is obtained by being a slave to virtue.

s: virtue is required for happiness
q: O girl, what happiness is there without virtue?

s: God's love is a dress and ornament (of the virtuous woman)
q: She maketh truth the parting of her hair, and love her dress and ornaments.

s: God owns the soul
q: Why forget Him who owneth thy soul and life?

s: pride causes impurity (in the heart)
q: What availeth it to bathe at the place of pilgrimage, if the filth of pride be in the heart?

s: pride remains in the heart (despite worldly offerings)
q: Were I to make large presents of lands and cows, even then pride would remain in my heart.

s: Death stands over man (without God's name)
q: Man's authority may be proclaimed throughout the whole world, but without the Name death standeth over his head.

s: the ocean of the world is dangerous and formidable (without shore or limit)
q: The fearful ocean of the world is dangerous and formidable; it hath no shore or limit,

s: the ocean of the world has no boat
q: No boat, no raft, no pole, and no boatman;

s: the ocean of the world is crossed by the holy (through God's name)
q: The perverse man perisheth in the terrible ocean of the world; the holy man crosseth it, unfathomable though it be.

s: the intoxicant illusion causes forgetfulness of death (in man)
q: In his intoxication he forgot death and enjoyed pleasure for four days.

s: the intoxicant illusion causes pleasure (temporary)
q: In his intoxication he forgot death and enjoyed pleasure for four days.

s: the boat is a means of crossing (the ocean of the world)
q: But the true Guru hath a vessel for the terrible ocean, and ferrieth over him on whom he looketh with favour.

s: the counterfeit is unacceptable (in God's treasury)
q: The counterfeit shall not be received in the great God's treasury, and they shall not behold Him.

s: God owns life
q: Why forget Him who owneth thy soul and life?

s: the counterfeit has no caste
q: The counterfeit have neither caste nor honour; the counterfeit are none of them acceptable.

s: the counterfeit has no honour
q: The counterfeit have neither caste nor honour; the counterfeit are none of them acceptable.

s: wealth is an entangling net (gold and silver)
q: Thou mayest amass gold and silver, but wealth is an entangling net.

s: the body is empty within (without love)
q: So the body which is empty within and possesseth no love, shall fall and become a heap of dust.

s: the body becomes a heap of dust (after falling)
q: So the body which is empty within and possesseth no love, shall fall and become a heap of dust.

s: the soul leaves the body (when the body falls)
q: When the body falleth, the soul fleeth away; what shall be the condition of the evil doers?

s: the heart contains God (through the Guru's instruction)
q: He is said to lead a happy life in whose heart God dwelleth through the Guru's instruction.

s: the mind is impure (when it is impure)
q: When the mind is impure the body is impure, and the tongue impure'.

s: religious ritual is inferior to the Name (even in great quantity)
q: Were I to perform hundreds of thousands and millions of religious ceremonies, all would not be equal to God's name.

s: God is inaccessible endless
q: Father, God is inaccessible and endless.

s: God consults no one (when He createth)
q: He consulteth no one when He createth; He consulteth no one when He destroyeth; He consulteth no one when He giveth or taketh.

s: God pervades men (within every heart)
q: God is the life within all lives; He pervadeth every heart.

s: God is life within men (within all lives)
q: God is the life within all lives; He pervadeth every heart.

s: God gives happiness (as Lord of the earth)
q: Arrange thine own affairs, O man; the Lord of the earth is the Giver of happiness.

s: God is omnipotent omnipotent
q: Thou art omnipotent; 1 have come into the world by Thy power.

s: God cools the world's fire (through God's name)
q: The world is fire, God's name is what cooleth it.

s: Guru gives instruction (through the Guru's words)
q: He on whom the Creator looketh with favour obtaineth instruction from the Guru's words.

s: Guru gives true merchandise (beneficently)
q: Day and night profit is obtained from God's name given by the beneficent Guru.

s: Guru gives God (through favour)
q: When by the Guru's favour man findeth God in his heart

s: Nanak is a writer (of the True Name)
q: Blest the writer, Nanak, who writeth the True Name.

s: Nanak is a dog (of God's court)
q: Nanak, the dog of Thy court, is growing madder every day for Thy love.

s: Nanak desires true merchandise (as his only request)
q: Grant me only one thing-Thy name; the poisonous things of the world please me not.

s: men has the body (as a palace, temple, and house of God)
q: The body is the palace, the temple, and the house of God;

s: men has the heart (as the place of divine realization)
q: When by the Guru's favour man findeth God in his heart

s: the pious are invited to God's palace
q: Nanak, the pious are invited to God's palace;

s: the pious are blended with God (in God's palace)
q: He will blend them with Himself.

s: the pious are absorbed in God (through the True One)
q: The pious who are absorbed in the True One shall be known in God's court.

s: true merchandise gives wisdom
q: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding are obtained from God's name;

s: true merchandise gives knowledge
q: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding are obtained from God's name;

s: true merchandise gives understanding
q: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding are obtained from God's name;

s: true merchandise profits men (day and night)
q: Day and night profit is obtained from God's name given by the beneficent Guru.

s: true merchandise cools the world's fire
q: The world is fire, God's name is what cooleth it.

s: the Word enables crossing the terrible ocean
q: Recognize the Word which will cause thee to cross the terrible ocean.

s: the heart contains God (God dwells within it)
q: The inaccessible and illimitable God dwelleth in man's heart.

s: the heart contains God's light (eternal)
q: The body is the palace, the temple, and the house of God; into it He putteth His eternal light.

s: the body is a palace (of God)
q: The body is the palace, the temple, and the house of God;

s: the body is a temple (of God)
q: The body is the palace, the temple, and the house of God;

s: the body is a house (of God)
q: The body is the palace, the temple, and the house of God;

s: world is a transient thing (like a flash of lightning)
q: The world is very transient like a flash of lightning;

s: God is a inaccessible and illimitable
q: The inaccessible and illimitable God dwelleth in man's heart.

s: world is a fire
q: The world is fire, God's name is what cooleth it.

s: woman is separated from God (when her Beloved liveth abroad)
q: Woman is separated from her Beloved who liveth abroad;

s: God dwells in the heart
q: The inaccessible and illimitable God dwelleth in man's heart.

s: wealth is a robber (of the world)
q: Empire, wealth, beauty, nobility, and youth are five robbers;

s: the grave is related to world (as the foolish heart fails to consider it)
q: Yet, foolish heart of mine, thou thinkest not of the grave.

s: fate is decided by God (according to God's order)
q: Man's fate is decided by God's order;

s: divine knowledge gives the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage (through bathing in immortal water)
q: He who batheth in the immortal water of divine knowledge taketh with him the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.

s: immortal water contains divine knowledge
q: He who batheth in the immortal water of divine knowledge taketh with him the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.

s: God gives wisdom (through God's name)
q: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding are obtained from God's name;

s: God gives knowledge (through God's name)
q: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding are obtained from God's name;

s: God gives understanding (through God's name)
q: Wisdom, knowledge, and understanding are obtained from God's name;

s: Jogis is a sect (twelvefold)
q: Jogis go to ruin in twelve sects

s: Bairagis is a perfect (when tinctured by the Word)
q: They who are tinctured by the Word are perfect Bairagis

s: Bairagis beg alms (to fix their love on God alone)
q: Who beg to obtain alms in the wallet of their hearts that their love may be fixed on God alone.

s: Bairagis love God (alone)
q: Who beg to obtain alms in the wallet of their hearts that their love may be fixed on God alone.

s: Guru gives instruction (to those who obtain it)
q: They who obtain the: Guru's instruction are pure

s: the Word contains religious ceremonies (along with purifications, austerities, devotion, penance, and pilgrimages)
q: All religious acts, purifications, austerities, devotion, penance, and pilgrimages abide in the Word.

s: religious ceremonies abide in the Word
q: All religious acts, purifications, austerities, devotion, penance, and pilgrimages abide in the Word.

s: Nanak teaches Guru (the true Guru unites man with God)
q: Nanak, if the true Guru be found, he will unite man with God, when sorrow and sin and death shall be no more.

s: Guru unites God (when the true Guru is found)
q: Nanak, if the true Guru be found, he will unite man with God

s: sin ends no more (when the true Guru unites man with God)
q: Nanak, if the true Guru be found, he will unite man with God, when sorrow and sin and death shall be no more.

s: death ends no more (when the true Guru unites man with God)
q: Nanak, if the true Guru be found, he will unite man with God, when sorrow and sin and death shall be no more.

s: religious ceremonies are vain vanity (except the repetition of the Name)
q: All religious acts are vain except the repetition of the Name

s: religious ceremonies require repetition of the Name (as their exception)
q: All religious acts are vain except the repetition of the Name

s: Jogis lack the Word (when without it)
q: The Jogis, the Kaprias, and the plucked-headed Saravagis without the Word have halters round their necks.

s: the Name contains six religious duties (the name of the Bright One)
q: The six religious duties are contained in the name of the Bright One.

s: Hindus consider ablution (of the Chandal and foul)
q: According to the Hindus foul is the ablution of the Chandal

s: Lord of the three worlds has flavour (which the impure man does not obtain)
q: In the impure man is pride; he obtaineth not the flavour of the Lord.

s: Kaprias lack the Word (when without it)
q: The Jogis, the Kaprias, and the plucked-headed Saravagis without the Word have halters round their necks.

s: Saravagis lack the Word (when without it)
q: The Jogis, the Kaprias, and the plucked-headed Saravagis without the Word have halters round their necks.

s: Jogis have halters (round their necks when without the Word)
q: The Jogis, the Kaprias, and the plucked-headed Saravagis without the Word have halters round their necks.

s: Sat Sangat is a Society of the holy
q: How is Sat Sangat, the Society of the holy, known?

s: man has shelter God (one shelter)
q: All creatures have one shelter, that of God.

s: God looks kindly at crane (conditionally)
q: What difference is there between a swan and a crane, if God look kindly on the latter?

s: God can change raven into swan
q: Nanak, if it please Him, He can change a raven into a swan,

s: Sat Sangat mentions name of God (the one God)
q: The name of the one God is mentioned there.

s: God is a one God
q: The name of the one God is mentioned there.

s: the Perfect One obtains sight of God
q: The perfect shall obtain a sight of God;

s: the fool has place with no place (with God)
q: the fool shall find no place with Him.

s: Guru is a Giver
q: The Guru is the Giver, the Guru is the house of snow, the Guru is the lamp of the three worlds.

s: God gives understanding (to those who understand)
q: He to whom God giveth understanding understandeth;

s: God gives knowledge (to those who know)
q: He to whom He giveth knowledge knoweth everything.

s: God controls man's power (giving and taking it away)
q: God it is who giveth man power and again taketh it away.

s: human life is a mansion of smoke (in Nanak's observation)
q: I, Nanak, have sought and searched, and seen that the world is a mansion of smoke.

s: human life is subject to birth and death (through worldly rejoicing and separation from God)
q: From worldly rejoicing proceedeth mourning, separation from God, birth, and death.

s: the soul departs the ocean of the world (at death)
q: The soul flieth away, showing the road of departure to others.

s: the ocean of the world is lost without Guru
q: Without a guru the world is lost.

s: the ocean of the world is deceived by falsehood (in its coming and going)
q: The whole world is deceived, and cometh and goeth in deception.

s: man's companions accompany the body (to the pyre with lamentations)
q: His companions accompany him to his pyre with loud lamentations.

s: Guru is a house of snow
q: The Guru is the Giver, the Guru is the house of snow, the Guru is the lamp of the three worlds.

s: mother is loved by human life (in its first stage)
q: In man's first stage he loveth the milk of his mother's breast;

s: father is recognized by human life (in its second stage)
q: In his second he recognizeth his father and mother

s: brother is recognized by human life (in its third stage)
q: In his third his brother, his brother's wife, and his own sister;

s: brother's wife is recognized by human life (in its third stage)
q: In his third his brother, his brother's wife, and his own sister;

s: sister is recognized by human life (in its third stage)
q: In his third his brother, his brother's wife, and his own sister;

s: the body is wasted by wrath (in old age)
q: In the eighth his body is wasted by wrath;

s: the mind is distracted by worldly occupations (when deceived by falsehood)
q: He who is deceived by false worldly occupations reacheth not God's palace: His heart is hard and he loseth his service.

s: pride is dispelled by the True Guru's instruction (under the Guru's instructions)
q: Nanak, when pride is dispelled under the Guru's instructions, man meditateth on God's name, Repeateth the Name, adoreth the Name, and through the Name is absorbed in happiness.

s: sin defiles the body (through sinful pleasure)
q: I am thoroughly defiled with sin, and desire to wash it away.

s: Guru is a lamp of the three worlds
q: The Guru is the Giver, the Guru is the house of snow, the Guru is the lamp of the three worlds.

s: the Name brings happiness (through meditation, repetition, and adoration)
q: Nanak, when pride is dispelled under the Guru's instructions, man meditateth on God's name, Repeateth the Name, adoreth the Name, and through the Name is absorbed in happiness.

s: the Word regenerates women (who adorn themselves with love and affection for their Spouse)
q: If women adorn themselves with love and affection for their Spouse, They shall not be restrained from their devotion to Him day or night. They shall abide in His chambers, and the Word shall regenerate them;

s: the Word removes doubt (for those to whom God gives it)
q: He Himself, Nanak, spoke the Word-- Doubt shall depart from him to whom He gave it.

s: the True Guru's instruction quenches greed (through the Guru's instruction)
q: In the heart is the fire of greed which is quenched by the Guru's instruction.

s: caste has no power (the reality is tested instead)
q: What power hath caste? It is the reality that is tested.

s: obedience to God's orders is a steed (sent into the world by the Master)
q: The Master sent obedience to His orders as a steed into the world;

s: the fool is unaffected by instruction (what is said is lost)
q: Nanak, the peculiarity of a fool is that what is said to him is ever lost.

s: greed is a fire (in the heart)
q: In the heart is the fire of greed which is quenched by the Guru's instruction.

s: wrath is a stream of fire (one of four destructive streams)
q: Cruelty, worldly love, avarice, and wrath are four streams of fire: They who fall into them are burnt.

s: worldly love is a stream of fire (one of four destructive streams)
q: Cruelty, worldly love, avarice, and wrath are four streams of fire: They who fall into them are burnt.

s: Guru possesses immortal wealth (through Nanak's statement)
q: Nanak, the Guru possesseth the immortal wealth; by putting faith in Him happiness is obtained.

s: the Guru's tree of contentment is a tree (of contentment)
q: Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment, whose blossom is religion and whose fruit is divine knowledge.

s: the Guru's tree of contentment has religion (as its blossom)
q: Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment, whose blossom is religion and whose fruit is divine knowledge.

s: the Guru's tree of contentment has divine knowledge (as its fruit)
q: Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment, whose blossom is religion and whose fruit is divine knowledge.

s: the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are at Guru (at the Guru's feet)
q: The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are at the Guru's feet, and ever specially worship them.

s: the minstrel is applied to God's work (by God)
q: Me, a minstrel out of work, God applieth to His work;

s: the minstrel sings God's praises (night and day by divine order)
q: He ordered me in the beginning to sing His praises night and day.

s: the minstrel obtains ambrosial food of the true Name (after receiving the robe of true praise)
q: The Master summoned the minstrel to His true court, And put on him a robe of true praise and eulogy: He then obtained the ambrosial food of the true Name.

s: God's court is a true court (belonging to the Master)
q: The Master summoned the minstrel to His true court,

s: Nanak seeks truth (through searching and observation)
q: I, Nanak, have sought and searched, and seen that the world is a mansion of smoke.

s: the Perfect One is obtained by true praise (through uttering and singing the Word)
q: Nanak, he who uttereth true praise obtaineth the Perfect One.

s: the Qazi practises falsehood (despite admonishing others)
q: All else is but worldly ostentation; thou, O Qazi, practisest falsehood.

s: Nanak is a minstrel (out of work before being summoned)
q: Me, a minstrel out of work, God applieth to His work;

s: God is a Creator
q: That which the Creator doeth cometh to pass; what man hath set in motion must stop.

s: God is a Giver (of maintenance and power)
q: Our maintenance is in nobody's power but God's:

s: God possesses all knowledge (as Commander)
q: The Commander, who created all things, Himself possesseth all knowledge.

s: fear of God is a fear (of God)
q: The fear of God is very great and very heavy.

s: God is Giver
q: Thou art the Giver, Thou art the Enjoyer, Thou art the support of the soul.

s: God is the support of the soul
q: Thou art the Giver, Thou art the Enjoyer, Thou art the support of the soul.

s: Guru is a teacher (spiritual guide)
q: He who can explain this is the Guru for me.

s: Guru shows God (to Nanak)
q: Saith Nanak, when the Guru showed me God, No one seemed to me to die or to be born.

s: Guru opens the heart (the adamant doors of understanding)
q: But by meeting the Guru the adamant doors of their understanding are opened.

s: Guru dispels doubts (of those whose works are true)
q: The Guru dispelleth the doubts of those whose works are true;

s: the Name is a nectar (in the heart and mouth)
q: The Name is nectar in the heart as well as in the mouth:

s: the Name frees man (from worldly desires)
q: Through it man is freed from worldly desires.

s: the Name delivers man (through meditation)
q: He is delivered by meditation on the Word and by God's name.

s: the Name is stock-in-trade (of Nanak)
q: I am a retail-dealer of Thine, O God; Thy Name is my stock-in-trade and my merchandise.

s: fear of God adorns man (through man's love)
q: No one shall be saved without the fear of God - His fear hath adorned man's love.

s: the Name is support (of Nanak)
q: The Name is my support; I shall abide as Thou keepest me, O Lord.

s: the Word is meditation object (for the pious)
q: He is delivered by meditation on the Word and by God's name.

s: the Word destroys pride (through the Guru's word)
q: He who meditateth on the Guru's word shall lose his pride;

s: man is a mortal (subject to death)
q: Whatever is created Death destroyeth.

s: man has the body (composed of wind, water, and fire)
q: The body is a mixture of wind, water, and fire;

s: man is born according to desires (of the heart)
q: Man is born according to the desires of his heart, and he is absorbed in the same way.

s: man is emancipated by the Name (when pious)
q: The pious man is emancipated and falleth into no entanglements: He is delivered by meditation on the Word and by God's name.

s: the soul is a conscious soul (immortal)
q: The conscious soul dieth not.

s: the soul does not die Death (when spiritual ignorance dies)
q: When my spiritual ignorance dieth, I die not myself.

s: fear of God fashions the Word (by fear)
q: By fear the Word is fashioned and decorated.

s: the body is a mixture (of wind, water, and fire)
q: The body is a mixture of wind, water, and fire;

s: the body has nine gates (and a tenth door)
q: The body hath nine gates and a tenth door; O wise man, understand and reflect on this.

s: the heart is changeful (within the body)
q: Within it is the changeful play of the intellect.

s: the heart is unstable (without God's essence)
q: But without being dyed with God's essence his mind is very unstable.

s: Death destroys man (all that is created)
q: Whatever is created Death destroyeth.

s: Death has net (over man's tongue, eyes, and ears)
q: The net of Death is over man's tongue and eyes; It is over his ears when he listeneth to unchaste language.

s: Death does not espy man (when God's true name dwells in the heart)
q: Death cannot espy him in whose heart God's true -name dwelleth, and who singeth God's praises--

s: mammon deludes man (including gods and goddesses)
q: Maya deludeth all the gods and goddesses.

s: Brahma is subject to Death (from the beginning)
q: Even Brahma was subject to death from the beginning.

s: the pious are associated with the Name (through spiritual fellowship)
q: They who are associated with the Name deem the world like a meeting-place of cowherds:

s: the pious are holy (God's perfect people)
q: A holy man is met by primal destiny. God's perfect people are rendered happy by truth

s: lust ruins man (with wrath)
q: He thinketh of lust and love for woman, Which with wrath ruin all sinners.

s: wrath ruins man (with lust)
q: He thinketh of lust and love for woman, Which with wrath ruin all sinners.

s: Nanak seeks Thy shelter (O God)
q: Nanak supplicateth, I seek Thy shelter, O God.

s: pride causes transmigration (through fetters of pride)
q: The fetters of pride cause man to wander in transmigration.

s: pride is removed by the Word (through meditation on the Guru's word)
q: He who meditateth on the Guru's word shall lose his pride;

s: woman is a young bride (separated from her Beloved)
q: Painful is the night for the young bride; without her Beloved she sleepeth not.

s: woman is unhonoured without God (without her beloved Lord)
q: The bride is unhonoured without her beloved Lord.

s: woman meets God (when He causes her to meet Him)
q: Nanak, she meeteth her Spouse when He causeth her to meet Him; without Him no sleep cometh to her.

s: woman is absorbed in God (through the Name)
q: Nanak, the woman who abandoneth not the Name shall be easily absorbed in God through it.

s: God is a Beloved (of the bride)
q: Painful is the night for the young bride; without her Beloved she sleepeth not.

s: God is recognized under Guru (by those with truth and contentment)
q: They in whose hearts there is truth and contentment, meet the Friend; under the Guru's instruction the Bridegroom is recognized.

s: God unites with woman (in love and dalliance)
q: Nanak, the Beloved and His spouse unite in dalliance; my desires have been fulfilled.

s: Nanak touches the feet of the pious (in reverence)
q: Nanak toucheth their feet.

s: wealth is impermanent (not taken beyond this world)
q: Arabian and Turkish steeds, gold, silver, and loads of raiment No one taketh with him; they leave him in this world, O fool.

s: God is a Lord (the one Lord)
q: It is the one Lord who saveth the three worlds; thou thinkest not of Him, O fool.

s: God is imperishable (invisible and inscrutable)
q: God is imperishable, invisible, and inscrutable.

s: God guards man (day and night)
q: So God day and night cherisheth and guardeth man and keepeth him in happiness.

s: God is the Spouse of all
q: Saith Nanak, God alone is the Spouse of all, She on whom He looketh with favour is the happy wife.

s: God grants salvation (through love)
q: Nanak, salvation is obtained by bearing love to God.

s: God is in world
q: And he shall behold God's form in the whole three worlds.

s: Nanak takes shelter in the Name
q: Nanak taketh shelter in God's name-- He whom the true Guru preserveth is freed from his entanglements.

s: Guru shows God (as the true Guru)
q: Nanak, the true Guru hath shown me God.

s: Guru gives the Name
q: God's name is wealth, the true Guru hath given it.

s: Guru leads to God's own abode
q: He who burneth his hopes and desires by the Word, Who uttereth and causeth others to utter God's name, Shall by means of the Guru find the way to God's own abode.

s: the True Guru's instruction removes worldly love
q: They who burn worldly love under the Guru's instruction, And ever meditate on the pure Name in their hearts, Hold and restrain their wandering minds.

s: the True Guru's instruction removes greed
q: Under the Guru's instruction greed is removed, and man arriveth at an understanding with God.

s: the Name is a wealth (that never fails)
q: I possess God's true name as wealth which shall never fail.

s: the Name removes pain
q: All pain shall be erased by the True Name

s: the Name delivers man (by God's favouring glance)
q: From the true Name--the kind Creator's name--honour is obtained. If it dwell day and night in the heart, O Nanak, man shall be delivered by God's favouring glance.

s: the Word is a means of devotion
q: He who burneth his hopes and desires by the Word, Who uttereth and causeth others to utter God's name, Shall by means of the Guru find the way to God's own abode.

s: worldly love binds the world (with many desires)
q: The world is bound by worldly love and many desires; Yet some reject it under the Guru's instruction.

s: worldly love causes transmigration
q: Through such love as that one is born again He who feeleth such love goeth to the city of Death.

s: God is a Creator
q: God acteth Himself and causeth to act.

s: worldly love is a sin (worldly)
q: Abandon worldly love; it is all sinful.

s: mammon causes forgetfulness of the Name
q: The fool loveth gold and woman; Attached to mammon he forgetteth the Name.

s: Death is not feared by those who have the Name within them
q: of the hearts of those who have the Name within them bloom, And they fear not Death

s: the mind wanders the forest of worldly love (like a furious elephant)
q: The apostate's mind is a furious elephant Which wandereth distracted in the forest of worldly love.
